The Kremlin said Moscow had shared what it knew and accused the media ​of spreading "false information".

items.title: China's evolving funeral practices: From traditional burials to cremation
items.desc: This year, China released new rules for funeral practices. The government is putting an emphasis on affordable and environmentally friendly funeral services. It's part of a decades-long reform to promote cremation. But in a country where burials are deeply rooted in local traditions, how are these attempts to modernise funerals being perceived? FRANCE 24's Yena Lee reports.

items.title: 'Great moral courage: The French thought they knew de Gaulle and suddenly realised they didn't'
items.desc: François Picard is pleased to welcome Julian Jackson, the British historian, author and Emeritus Professor of Modern French History at Queen Mary University of London. His biography of Charles de Gaulle laid the foundation for France's two-part biopic, "De Gaulle: Résistance". And on the heels of that surprise box-office hit, Jackson's book is now available in French as "La Chute : France, 1940". He takes us back to the occupation of Paris and the extraordinary collapse of France in the summer of 1940.

items.title: October 7: Former Israeli hostage speaks to France 24
items.desc:
“The terrorists pulled us out through the window. They handcuffed me and pushed us into a car that they had brought from Gaza.”
 
Former Israeli hostage Shoshan Haran speaks to France 24.

items.title: French parents join school protests to support and protect their children
items.desc: Widespread protests swept across France on Tuesday over anger at the state of the country's school system. The police responded with tear gas and water canons when some on the fringes of the marches turned violent. Among the demonstrators were parents who came to march alongside their children to support their cause – and, for some, to ensure their children could protest safely. After several teenagers were injured, they feared further clashes.

items.title: Three years on, October 7 massacre sites in Israel draw visitors seeking to remember
items.desc: Three years after the October 7 attack, when Hamas militants killed at least 1,195 people in Israel – mostly civilians – the sites of the massacre near the Gaza border have become heavily visited memorials. They offer Israelis and Jews in the diaspora a place to honour those who were killed, as FRANCE 24’s Stéphane Amar reports.

items.title: Three years on, questions remain over what Netanyahu knew before October 7
items.desc: As Israelis mark the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack, and with elections due later this month, one question keeps resurfacing: What did Benjamin Netanyahu know in the run-up to the attack? The Israeli prime minister has been accused of ignoring repeated warnings – an allegation he denies.

items.title: Devastation in Gaza: Three years of war reshape the enclave beyond recognition
items.desc: Three years ago, the war between Israel and Hamas began. In Gaza, it has meant three years of bombardment that have dramatically transformed the Palestinian territory. Residents of the enclave try to survive the best they can, caught between hope for a better future and resignation.
